details:
COSMO CLASS - Planet X Hunter | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

Built by A. DISAS DINSITHA, Age 12, from Bandaragama, Sri Lanka.

Is there a ninth planet beyond Neptune?

Planet X is a hypothesized, extremely cold world that may orbit far beyond Neptune. It is too faint to see easily, so astronomers must compare sky-survey images taken months apart and look for a tiny moving dot against stationary stars.

COSMO CLASS turns that complex idea into a hands-on investigation for everyone.

WHAT YOU CAN DO:

1. EXPLORE 102 SPHEREx BANDS

Browse all 102 SPHEREx infrared bands from 0.75 to 5.00 microns. Use keyboard controls, timelapse, and Audio Sonar to hear the data.

2. BLINK COMPARATOR

Compare Survey 1 (March 2025) vs Survey 2 (September) like Clyde Tombaugh did when he found Pluto. Spot the moving red-dot candidate against stationary stars.

3. EXPERIMENT LAB

Adjust detection threshold, observation range (1-100 AU), motion sensitivity, and bandpass filters. Watch 12 raw triggers get filtered to 4 confirmed candidates, with 67% noise reduction.

4. 6-STAGE AI PIPELINE

Ingestion → Calibration → Motion Detection → False-Positive Pruning → Ranking → Human Review. AI helps, but a human scientist always makes the final decision.

5. This project also features two main educational blogs — "HISTORY OF PLANET X" and "🌌 HOW DID NASA DISCOVER NEW STARS AND PLANETS?" — which help students understand the history, science, and discovery methods behind Planet X and other celestial objects.

COSMO CLASS PRODUCT ECOSYSTEM - 11 TOOLS:

A comprehensive suite of 11 interactive digital platforms created by 12-year-old developer A. Disas Dinsitha (Bandaragama, Sri Lanka), spanning 3D planetary exploration, NASA AI learning, voice accessibility, code sandboxes, and logic games.

1. Hela Scope – Explore 3D Planets - Explore planets in our Solar System in an immersive 3D environment while learning new facts about space.

2. Solar System Eyes – Explore the Solar System - Explore information about the Solar System and its planets in an enjoyable way for students and space enthusiasts.

3. EDU DINSI – Blind Mode - Listen to news and information from the website. Designed for users who may find it difficult to view the screen or for anyone who prefers to listen.

4. EDU DINSI – Educational & News Platform - Read educational content, news, and informative articles.

5. EDU DSL – NASA Space Articles & Blogs - Read educational articles and blogs about NASA and space science.

6. CODE DIMEX – HTML, CSS & JavaScript Testing - Write, run, and test HTML, CSS, and JavaScript code and instantly view the results.

7. Questions & Quiz – Test Your Knowledge - Answer a variety of questions and test knowledge. Includes Quiz Master Sri Lanka + Science Quiz Explorer.

8. Quiz Master Sri Lanka - National-level astronomy and space science quiz with multiple-choice questions, timers, and scoring.

9. MoodREV – Text Document Maker - Simple text document editor for creating and editing documents.

10. Rocket Game - Action-packed asteroid avoidance rocket game testing quick reflexes and navigation in deep space.

11. Developer Portfolio – Certificates & Projects - Showcases certificates, projects, websites, and other technology-related work.

12. Genie AI Chatbot & Open Source Repository - Explore the advanced commercial chatbot and open-source GitHub code backing the COSMO CLASS suite.

HOW WE USE NASA DATA:

This project is an educational simulation inspired by NASA data. We studied how real SPHEREx data is accessed using the official SPHEREx Tutorial Notebooks, which show how to use Python to explore SPHEREx spectral images. The real data archive is the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) for SPHEREx. Our Blink Comparator design was inspired by WiseView, a tool used in the Backyard Worlds: Planet 9 project to find moving objects. We use Gaia Data Release 3 to identify known stars and filter them out.

DATA & SOURCES

1. SPHEREx Tutorial Notebooks - Caltech / IPAC Python Guides

https://caltech-ipac.github.io/irsa-tutorials/tutorials/spherex/spherex_intro.html

We studied how to use Python to explore SPHEREx spectral images.

2. NASA/IPAC IRSA SPHEREx Archive - Official Mission Data Archive

https://irsa.ipac.caltech.edu/Missions/spherex.html

Real data archive for SPHEREx. IRSA is the primary archive for SPHEREx data.

3. WiseView - Backyard Worlds Blink Tool

http://byw.tools/wiseview

Our Blink Comparator design was inspired by WiseView, a tool used in Backyard Worlds: Planet 9 to find moving objects.

4. Gaia Data Release 3 - ESA Star Catalog Archive

https://archives.esac.esa.int/gaia

We use Gaia DR3 to identify known stars and filter them out.

5. NEOSSat - CSA / Canadian Astronomy Data Centre

https://www.cadc-ccda.hia-iha.nrc-cnrc.gc.ca/en/neosat/

Learn about NEOSSat, Canada's space telescope for asteroids, comets, satellites, and space debris.

6. Canadian Astronomy Data Centre (CADC)

https://www.cadc-ccda.hia-iha.nrc-cnrc.gc.ca/en/

Access to astronomical observations from Canadian and international telescopes.

WHY IT MATTERS:

The data does not change the object, it changes our decision. Gaia DR3 removes known stars. SPHEREx checks temperature - Planet X should be very cold (~40K). WiseView checks motion - if it doesn't move in 6 months, it's a distant star. Tutorial Notebooks help remove camera noise.

Designed to be Seen, Read, Heard, Played, and Built - by everyone. Built for students, teachers, and curious minds everywhere.

DISCLAIMER:

This project is an educational simulation. It does not claim a real discovery or confirmation of Planet X. NASA does not endorse this project.

Built with Google AI Studio, with student design, verification, and testing.

Science for everyone.
